en: An act of fighting against a government or ruler, usually by many people.
ex: The army crushed the uprising within a week.
軍隊在一週內鎮壓了這場起義。

en: Suggested but not directly stated; or being a natural part of something.
ex: There was an implicit threat in his words.
他的話裡帶有隱含的威脅。

en: Strong-smelling smoke or gas; or to be very angry.
ex: The factory released harmful fumes into the air.
工廠向空氣中排放有害的煙氣。

en: To hear what other people are saying without them knowing.
ex: I overheard them talking about the surprise party.
我無意中聽到他們在談論驚喜派對。

en: To save something from being destroyed or lost; or the things saved.
ex: Divers salvaged valuable items from the sunken ship.
潛水員從沉船中打撈出貴重物品。

en: Having attractive natural views.
ex: We took the scenic route along the coast.
我們走了沿海的風景路線。

en: A short, high sound made by a small bird or insect; or to make such a sound.
ex: We woke up to the chirp of birds outside the window.
我們被窗外的鳥鳴聲吵醒。

en: Careful and detailed examination of something, especially by the public or an official.
ex: The company's accounts came under close scrutiny.
這家公司的帳目受到嚴格審查。

en: A person who plays the piano.
ex: The pianist received a standing ovation after the concert.
鋼琴家在音樂會結束後獲得全場起立鼓掌。

en: To show approval by clapping your hands; or to praise something publicly.
ex: The audience applauded for five minutes.
觀眾鼓掌長達五分鐘。

en: The start of something.
col: at the outset of the project
make it clear from the outset
ex: I made it clear from the outset that I disagreed.
我從一開始就表明了我不同意。

en: Old and in poor condition; or unfair and unkind.
ex: The old man wore a shabby coat full of holes.
那位老人穿著一件滿是破洞的舊外套。

en: To make something stronger or more intense; or to become higher.
ex: The incident heightened tensions between the two countries.
這起事件加劇了兩國之間的緊張關係。

en: The act of winning control of a place or people by force; or something won this way.
ex: The Spanish conquest of the Americas began in the 1500s.
西班牙對美洲的征服始於十六世紀。

en: To make a person or society more developed in culture and behavior.
ex: We should behave in a civilized way even when we disagree.
即使意見不同，我們也應該文明地行事。

en: To trouble or annoy someone repeatedly, or to treat them in an unpleasant way, often sexually.
ex: Employees have the right to work without being harassed.
員工有權在不受騷擾的環境中工作。

en: A number of things that follow one another; or the right to take over a position after someone.
ex: Three accidents happened in quick succession.
三起事故接連發生。

en: Homosexual (now the most common meaning); or, in older use, cheerful and lively.
ex: The city holds a gay pride parade every year.
這座城市每年都舉辦同志驕傲大遊行。

en: To make someone unable to see for a short time by a bright light; or to impress someone very much.
ex: The bright headlights dazzled the driver.
明亮的車頭燈讓駕駛眼花。

en: To feed on grass in a field; or to lightly scrape the skin; or a slight wound.
ex: Cows were grazing peacefully in the meadow.
牛群在草地上悠閒地吃草。

en: Not wearing any clothes; or a painting or photo of a person without clothes.
ex: The museum has a famous nude painting by Titian.
博物館藏有提香一幅有名的裸體畫。

en: Not allowing air to get in or out; or so strong that no weakness can be found.
ph: 無懈可擊的不在場證明
ex: Store the cookies in an airtight container to keep them fresh.
把餅乾存放在密封容器裡以保持新鮮。

en: Thinking carefully about things; or able to send back light, heat or sound.
ex: The cyclists wore reflective jackets at night.
騎自行車的人晚上穿著反光外套。

en: Making you feel tired or bored; or annoying.
ex: Waiting in line all day was a tiresome experience.
整天排隊是件累人的事。

en: A high-ranking officer in the navy who commands a fleet or a group of ships.
ex: The admiral ordered the fleet to set sail at dawn.
上將下令艦隊於黎明起航。

en: To feel or show great joy about something good that has happened.
ex: The whole town rejoiced when the war ended.
戰爭結束時，全鎮都歡欣鼓舞。

en: For a short period of time.
ex: Let's sit and rest awhile before we continue.
我們坐下來休息一會兒再繼續吧。

en: Based on personal opinions or feelings rather than facts.
ex: Taste in art is highly subjective.
對藝術的品味是非常主觀的。

en: An activity that you do regularly for pleasure in your free time.
ex: Reading is her favorite pastime.
閱讀是她最喜歡的消遣。

en: The branch of mathematics that deals with shapes, lines, angles and space.
ex: We learned about triangles and circles in geometry class.
我們在幾何課學到三角形和圓形。

en: A person or thing that has the same position or function as another in a different place or organization.
ex: The prime minister met his German counterpart yesterday.
首相昨天會見了他的德國對等官員。

en: The length of time that something lasts or continues.
ex: The film is about two hours in duration.
這部電影長約兩小時。

en: Relating to the cells of living things; or relating to mobile phones that use a network of areas called cells.
ex: Scientists study the cellular structure of plants.
科學家研究植物的細胞結構。

en: To walk in a slow, relaxed way; or a slow, relaxed walk.
ex: We took a stroll along the beach after dinner.
晚餐後我們沿著海灘散步。

en: To use your strength, influence or ability to make something happen.
ex: The government exerted pressure on the company to change.
政府向這家公司施壓要求改變。

en: Having a limit or an end; not infinite.
ex: The Earth's natural resources are finite.
地球的自然資源是有限的。

en: Materials for writing, such as paper, pens and envelopes; or the shop that sells them.
ex: She bought some pens and notebooks at the stationery shop.
她在文具店買了一些筆和筆記本。

en: To force someone to do something because of a law or duty; or to help someone by doing a favor.
ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
法律規定駕駛必須繫安全帶。

en: A large amount of money given to an institution; or a natural ability or talent.
ex: The university received a large endowment from a former graduate.
大學收到一位校友的大筆捐贈。

en: The force or speed of movement that increases as something moves; or the power to keep developing.
ex: The campaign is gaining momentum across the country.
這項運動正在全國範圍內獲得動力。
